knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bienert_2025_sufentanil"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bienert_2025_sufentanil"))$description`
* Article: [Clin Pharmacokinet 2025;64(9):1331-1340](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-025-01543-y)

Sufentanil given into the epidural space reaches plasma slowly, and its plasma
concentrations decline more slowly than after intravenous dosing. Bienert 2025
explains this with a two-compartment absorption site: the dose enters an
epidural absorption compartment (`depot`, the paper's A1) that drains quickly
into plasma (KA) and also exchanges quickly with an epidural distribution
compartment (`depot_peripheral`, the paper's A4, attributed to epidural fat)
from which sufentanil returns only slowly (KA41). Disposition is a standard
two-compartment model. Because the slow return from the epidural fat is slower
than sufentanil's own terminal disposition, the post-infusion decline is
absorption-limited (flip-flop kinetics).

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bienert_2025_sufentanil"))
mod
```

# Population

Bienert 2025 studied 23 adults (12 female, 11 male; ASA physical status 2 in 9
and 3 in 14 patients) undergoing major oncologic or non-oncologic abdominal
surgery under general anaesthesia combined with epidural analgesia at a single
centre in Poznan, Poland (NCT06069219). The abstract gives an age range of
30-83 years; Table S1 reports a median (IQR) age of 60 (42.5-65) years and body
weight of 71 (59-80.5) kg. The epidural catheter sat between Th8/9 and Th12/L1.
After an initial epidural dose of sufentanil with an amide local anaesthetic,
sufentanil was infused epidurally, titrated to response, during surgery and for
the following 3 days (median intra-operative epidural dose 15 ug, Table S1).
Plasma was sampled densely during the infusion and for 72 h after it stopped.

Age, weight, height, sex and catheter placement were explored only graphically
against the individual random effects (Figures S5-S9); no covariate model was
fitted, so the model has no covariates.

```{r population}
pop <- mod$population
str(pop[c("species", "n_subjects", "age_range", "age_median", "weight_median", "sex_female_pct")])
```

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ODE system (A1, A4, C1, C2) | as in `model()` | Statistical Methods, final model equations; K matrix of the deposited Stan code (`model/torsten/3b/3b.stan`) |
| Concentration = amount / V1 x 1000 (pg/mL) | | Deposited Stan code (`x[2] ./ theta[3] .* 1000`) |
| `lcl` | 64.9 L/h | Table 1, thetaCL mean |
| `lq` | 48.2 L/h | Table 1, thetaQ mean |
| `lvc` | 10.2 L | Table 1, thetaV1 mean |
| `lvp` | 506 L | Table 1, thetaV2 mean |
| `lka` | 3.27 1/h | Table 1, thetaKA mean |
| `lka14` | 14.9 1/h | Table 1, thetaKA14 mean |
| `lka41` | 0.14 1/h | Table 1, thetaKA41 mean |
| IIV SDs (log scale) | 0.49, 0.45, 1.51, 0.41, 0.36, 0.38, 0.5 | Table 1, omega CL, Q, V1, V2, KA, KA14, KA41 means |
| IIV correlations | 21 posterior-mean rho | Deposited `deliv/tables/torsten/3b/parameters-table.csv` |
| Omega = diag(omega) rho diag(omega) | | Statistical Methods |
| `expSd` | 0.31 | Table 1, sigma mean |
| `nu` | 3.81 | Table 1, nu mean |
| Student-t residual on log(C) | | Statistical Methods |

# Replicating Figure S10: dosing to an epidural steady state

The Discussion derives a regimen that puts the epidural absorption compartment
at its steady-state amount from the start: an induction dose of `Rss / KA`
followed by an infusion whose rate decays as
`Rss + KA14 / KA * Rss * exp(-KA41 * t)`. With that input, `depot` holds
exactly at `Rss / KA` (the KA14 outflow is replaced by the decaying extra rate)
while the epidural fat fills, and plasma approaches `Rss / CL`. Figure S10 shows
this for `Rss = 3` ug/h in the typical subject. The decaying rate is given here
as consecutive 0.05-h infusions, each carrying the exact integral of the rate
over its interval.

```{r figS10}
typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
ka <- exp(mod$theta[["lka"]])
ka14 <- exp(mod$theta[["lka14"]])
ka41 <- exp(mod$theta[["lka41"]])
cl <- exp(mod$theta[["lcl"]])
rss <- 3
dt_seg <- 0.05
t_seg <- seq(0, 72 - dt_seg, by = dt_seg)
seg_amt <- rss * dt_seg +
  (ka14 / ka) * rss / ka41 * (exp(-ka41 * t_seg) - exp(-ka41 * (t_seg + dt_seg)))

ev_s10 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = rss / ka, rate = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = t_seg, amt = seg_amt, rate = seg_amt / dt_seg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.25), amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
)
sim_s10 <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev_s10, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
  as.data.frame()

rate_df <- data.frame(time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.25)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(value = rss + (ka14 / ka) * rss * exp(-ka41 * time), panel = "Infusion rate (ug/h)")
plot_s10 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rate_df,
  sim_s10 |> dplyr::transmute(time, value = depot, panel = "Epidural absorption compartment (ug)"),
  sim_s10 |> dplyr::transmute(time, value = Cc, panel = "Plasma concentration (pg/mL)")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c(
    "Infusion rate (ug/h)", "Epidural absorption compartment (ug)", "Plasma concentration (pg/mL)"
  )))

ggplot(plot_s10, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, caption = "Replicates Figure S10 of Bienert 2025 (typical subject, Rss = 3 ug/h).") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figS10-check}
s10_at <- sim_s10 |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(20, 40, 72)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, depot, Cc)
# Figure S10 plasma curve, read off the published panel at 20, 40 and 72 h.
s10_at$Cc_fig <- c(39.5, 44.5, 46)
knitr::kable(s10_at, digits = 3, caption = "Typical-subject Figure S10 values.")

c(
  initial_rate = rss * (1 + ka14 / ka),
  initial_rate_ratio = 1 + ka14 / ka,
  depot_target = rss / ka,
  plasma_ss = 1000 * rss / cl
)

stopifnot(
  # depot is held at Rss / KA by construction. The decaying rate is given as
  # 0.05-h constant-rate steps, which leaves a ripple of a few 1e-4.
  all(abs(sim_s10$depot[sim_s10$time > 0] / (rss / ka) - 1) < 2e-3),
  # Plasma curve matches the published panel.
  all(abs(s10_at$Cc / s10_at$Cc_fig - 1) < 0.10),
  # The paper's 'initial dose rate must be about 5.5 higher'.
  abs((1 + ka14 / ka) - 5.5) < 0.2,
  # Plasma approaches Rss / CL (46.2 pg/mL) by 72 h.
  abs(s10_at$Cc[s10_at$time == 72] / (1000 * rss / cl) - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The induction dose of `3 / 3.27 = 0.92` ug keeps the absorption compartment flat,
the starting rate is `3 x (1 + 14.9 / 3.27) = 16.7` ug/h (Figure S10 starts just
under 17 ug/h; the Discussion's "about 5.5 higher"), and plasma rises from about
27 pg/mL at 1 h towards `1000 x 3 / 64.9 = 46.2` pg/mL, as in Figure S10.

# Half-lives of the absorption and disposition processes

The Discussion reports the beta-phase half-life of absorption as 29.7 +/- 5.8 h
and of disposition as 13.7 +/- 3.4 h (posterior mean +/- SD of the half-lives
computed from each draw of the typical values). The same bi-exponential formula
applied to the posterior-mean typical values gives:

```{r half-lives}
q <- exp(mod$theta[["lq"]])
vc <- exp(mod$theta[["lvc"]])
vp <- exp(mod$theta[["lvp"]])
beta_rate <- function(k_out, k_fwd, k_back) {
  s <- k_out + k_fwd + k_back
  0.5 * (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k_back * k_out))
}
thalf_abs <- log(2) / beta_rate(ka, ka14, ka41)
thalf_dis <- log(2) / beta_rate(cl / vc, q / vc, q / vp)
data.frame(
  process = c("absorption (beta)", "disposition (beta)"),
  model_h = c(thalf_abs, thalf_dis),
  paper_mean_h = c(29.7, 13.7),
  paper_sd_h = c(5.8, 3.4)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  abs(thalf_abs - 29.7) < 5.8,
  abs(thalf_dis - 13.7) < 3.4,
  # Flip-flop: absorption is the slower process.
  thalf_abs > thalf_dis
)
```

The half-lives from the mean typical values sit slightly below the paper's
means, as expected when the paper averages a non-linear function over posterior
draws; both are well inside one posterior SD.

# Virtual cohort and visual predictive check

The study regimens were individually titrated (the authors' deposited dataset
shows maintenance infusion rates mostly between 0.75 and 3 ug/h, short faster
segments of 15-150 ug/h for the initial and supplementary doses, and total
infusion durations of 12-74 h), so an exact replication of the Figure 4
VPC is not possible from the published material. As an illustration, 200
virtual patients receive a representative regimen of 10 ug over 10 min followed
by 1.5 ug/h for 48 h, sampled on the study's schedule during and for 72 h after
the infusion. The model has no covariates, so no covariate distribution is
needed.

```{r vpc}
obs_during <- c(5 / 60, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, 47.9)
obs_post <- 48 + c(3, 5, 20, 40) / 60
obs_post <- c(obs_post, 48 + c(1, 2, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72))
ev_vpc <- rxode2::et(amt = 10, rate = 60, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(time = 1 / 6, amt = 1.5 * (48 - 1 / 6), rate = 1.5, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(sort(unique(c(obs_during, obs_post))), cmt = "central")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250629)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc, nSub = 200) |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(phase = ifelse(time < 48, "During infusion", "Post infusion"),
                tplot = ifelse(time < 48, time, time - 48)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(phase, tplot) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), p90 = quantile(sim, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(tplot)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~phase, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Sufentanil concentration (pg/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles (with residual error);",
      "compare with the layout of Figure 4B of Bienert 2025."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated median rises from a few pg/mL in the first hours to about
10-20 pg/mL at 24-48 h and falls to a few pg/mL 72 h after the infusion stops,
the same range as the observed median in Figure 4B.

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the same regimen without residual error (IIV
retained), split into the infusion interval (0-48 h) and the post-infusion
interval (48-120 h). The paper reports no NCA, so the only published comparator
is the terminal half-life: under flip-flop kinetics the late post-infusion
decline should approach the absorption beta-phase half-life (29.7 h).

```{r pknca}
# Cc is the individual prediction (IIV, no residual error); the
# residual-error draw is in the separate `sim` column.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250630)
ev_nca <- rxode2::et(amt = 10, rate = 60, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(time = 1 / 6, amt = 1.5 * (48 - 1 / 6), rate = 1.5, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 1), 48 + c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72)))), cmt = "central")
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_nca, nSub = 200) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::rename(id = sim.id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "10 ug + 1.5 ug/h x 48 h")

conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = rep(unique(conc_df$id), each = 2),
  time = rep(c(0, 1 / 6), times = length(unique(conc_df$id))),
  amt = rep(c(10, 1.5 * (48 - 1 / 6)), times = length(unique(conc_df$id))),
  treatment = "10 ug + 1.5 ug/h x 48 h"
)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "pg/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "ug")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 48),
  end = c(48, 120),
  cmax = c(TRUE, TRUE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  treatment = "10 ug + 1.5 ug/h x 48 h",
  half.life = 29.7
)
hl_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", start == 48) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = hl_sim,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "half.life",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Post-infusion terminal half-life: simulated (median) vs the paper's absorption beta-phase half-life. * marks rows differing by >20%.")

stopifnot(abs(median(hl_sim$PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE) / 29.7 - 1) < 0.2)
```

The post-infusion terminal half-life of the simulated cohort is close to the
paper's absorption beta-phase half-life and well above the disposition
beta-phase half-life (13.7 h), which is the flip-flop behaviour the model was
built to describe.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Posterior means as point estimates.** Table 1 reports the posterior mean and
  median of each parameter. The model uses the means, which are the values the
  paper itself uses for the typical subject (Discussion: CL 64.9 L/h,
  `Rss / KA` approximately `Rss / 3.3`, KA14 / KA approximately 4.5).
- **IIV correlations from the authors' deposit.** The paper estimates a full
  7 x 7 correlation matrix (LKJ(10) prior) but prints only the SDs. The
  correlations are the posterior means in the authors' public output for the
  same final model (`deliv/tables/torsten/3b/parameters-table.csv` of
  github.com/wiczling/sufentanil-epidural). Only the CL-V1 correlation (0.25)
  has a 90% interval excluding zero; the rest are near zero. The assembled
  covariance matrix is positive definite. The SDs are the Table 1 values, which
  match the deposit to two significant figures.
- **KA41 rounding.** Table 1 prints the KA41 mean as 0.14 1/h; the deposit gives
  0.135 1/h. The model uses the printed 0.14.
- **Residual error.** The paper fits `log(Cobs)` with a Student-t error of scale
  sigma and nu degrees of freedom. This is encoded as `lnorm(expSd) + dt(nu)`;
  rxode2 uses the same scale parameterisation as Stan. `nu` is the paper's name
  for the degrees of freedom. No canonical name exists for a t-distribution
  degrees-of-freedom parameter, so `checkModelConventions()` warns that `nu` is
  not one of `propSd` / `addSd` / `expSd`; the warning is expected.
- **Epidural distribution compartment.** The paper's A4 exchanges only with the
  epidural absorption compartment, never with plasma, a role no registered
  compartment name covers (`abs_site` exchanges with `central`; `depot2` denotes
  a second dosing route). It is named `depot_peripheral` and declared in the
  model's `paper_specific_compartments`. The paper's own rate-constant names
  KA14 and KA41 are kept (`ka14`, `ka41`).
- **Bioavailability.** The model assumes complete absorption from the epidural
  space, as the paper does (Discussion); CL and the volumes are therefore
  apparent values relative to the epidural dose.
- **Illustrative regimen.** The VPC and NCA regimen (10 ug over 10 min, then
  1.5 ug/h for 48 h) is representative of, not identical to, the individually
  titrated study regimens, so the VPC is a qualitative comparison with
  Figure 4B.
- **Number of subjects.** The paper describes 23 patients; the deposited
  analysis dataset contains concentration records for 18 of them. The paper
  does not state that any patient was excluded, and the population metadata
  reports the 23 described.
